4395.stem:
A university uses gas to heat its buildings. Over a period of 10 weekdays during winter, the gas used each day was measured in megawatts (MW) and the average outside temperature each day was recorded in degrees Celsius ($^\circ$C).

Using $x$ as the average daily outside temperature and $y$ as the total daily gas usage, the equation of the least-squares regression line was found.

The equation of the regression line predicts that when the temperature is $0^\circ$C, the daily gas usage is 236 MW.

The ten temperatures measured were: $0^\circ, 0^\circ, 0^\circ, 2^\circ, 5^\circ, 7^\circ, 8^\circ, 9^\circ, 9^\circ, 10^\circ$.

The total gas usage for the ten weekdays was 1840 MW.

In any bivariate dataset, the least-squares regression line passes through the point $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$, where $\bar{x}$ is the sample mean of the $x$-values and $\bar{y}$ is the sample mean of the $y$-values.

figures.cap: blank grid of daily gas usage against average temperature
solution sketch: grid with points (0,236) and (5,184) plotted

parts.latex:
Using the information provided, plot the point $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$ and the $y$-intercept of the least-squares regression line on the grid.

\exfigure{300_q34_1}
What is the equation of the regression line?
In the context of the dataset, identify ONE problem with using the regression line to predict gas usage when the average outside temperature is $23^\circ$C.

solutions.latex:
The mean temperature is the sum divided by 10.
$$\begin{aligned}\bar{x} &= \dfrac{0+0+0+2+5+7+8+9+9+10}{10}\\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\bar{y} &= \dfrac{1840}{10}\\ &= 184\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ (\bar{x},\bar{y}) = (5,184)$$
The $y$-intercept is $(0, 236)$.

\exfigure{300_q34_s1}
criteria: Correctly plots both points on the graph
Calculates $\bar{x}$ and $\bar{y}$, and plots this point on the grid, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Sketch still to draw: on the question's grid (x = temperature, y = gas usage), plot and label the point (5, 184) and the y-intercept (0, 236). The existing figure key 300_q34_s1 is kept.

solutions.latex:
The line passes through $(0,236)$ and $(5,184)$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Slope} &= \dfrac{184-236}{5-0}\\ &= -10.4\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ y = 236-10.4x$$
criteria: Finds the slope of the regression line, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
At $23^\circ$C the equation gives $y = 236-10.4\times 23 = -3.2$.

This is negative gas usage, which is not physically possible.
criteria: Identifies one problem with predicting using the regression line

meta.format_note: Added the line y = -3.2 to support the source's statement.

parts.latex:
For a particular course, the recorded data show a relationship between the number of hours of study per week and the marks achieved out of 100.

A least-squares regression line is fitted to this dataset. The equation of this line is given by

$$M = 20 + 3H,$$

where $M$ is the predicted mark and $H$ is the number of hours of study per week.

Based on this regression equation, which of the following is correct regarding the predicted mark of a student?

solutions.latex:
In $M = 20 + 3H$, the intercept is 20 and the gradient is 3.

When $H=0$:
$$M = 20 + 3(0) = 20$$
So the predicted mark is 20 for zero hours of study, which is option B.

The gradient 3 means the predicted mark increases by 3 for each additional hour. So A, C and D are incorrect.

parts.latex:
A cricket is an insect. The male cricket produces a chirping sound.

A scientist wants to explore the relationship between the temperature in degrees Celsius and the number of cricket chirps heard in a 15-second time interval.

Once a day for 20 days, the scientist collects data. Based on the 20 data points, the scientist provides the information below.

\begin{itemize}
\item A box-plot of the temperature data is shown.

\exfigure{36_q36_1}
\item The mean temperature in the dataset is $0.525^\circ\text{C}$ below the median temperature in the dataset.
\item A total of 684 chirps was counted when collecting the 20 data points.
\end{itemize}

The scientist fits a least-squares regression line using the data $(x, y)$, where $x$ is the temperature in degrees Celsius and $y$ is the number of chirps heard in a 15-second time interval. The equation of this line is

$$y = -10.6063 + bx,$$

where $b$ is the slope of the regression line.

The least-squares regression line passes through the point $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$ where $\bar{x}$ is the sample mean of the temperature data and $\bar{y}$ is the sample mean of the chirp data.

Calculate the number of chirps expected in a 15-second interval when the temperature is $19^\circ$ Celsius. Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.

solutions.latex:
The median temperature is $22$, read from the box-plot, so
$$\bar{x} = 22-0.525 = 21.475$$
$$\bar{y} = \dfrac{684}{20} = 34.2$$
The regression line passes through $(\bar{x},\bar{y})$:
$$\begin{aligned} 34.2 &= -10.6063+b(21.475) \\ b &= \dfrac{44.8063}{21.475} \\ &= 2.08644\ldots \end{aligned}$$
When $x=19$:
$$\begin{aligned} y &= -10.6063+2.08644\ldots\times 19 \\ &= 29.03606\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 29 \text{ chirps are expected}$$
criteria: Finds value of $b$, or equivalent merit
Substitutes $\bar{x}$ and $\bar{y}$ into the regression equation, or equivalent merit
Finds the value of $\bar{x}$ and $\bar{y}$, or equivalent merit
Finds the value of $\bar{x}$ or $\bar{y}$ or the median of the temperature, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Median 22 taken from the box-plot as in the source.

parts.latex: Identify the independent variable and dependent variable in this situation.
Calculate Pearson's correlation coefficient ($r$) for the relationship between the average hours of sleep per day and average attention span. Give your answer correct to four decimal places.

With reference to Pearson's correlation coefficient calculated in part (b), describe the strength and direction of the correlation of the relationship between the average hours of sleep per day and average attention span.
Find the equation of the least-squares regression line, for the given data correct to four decimal places.

Using the graph's regression line, predict the average attention span, in minutes, for a student who gets an average of 12 hours of sleep per day and state whether your prediction is interpolation or extrapolation.
Using the gradient of the regression line found in part (d), explain what it represents in the context of this study.

In the context of this dataset, identify one limitation of using the regression line to predict the average hours of sleep for a student with an average attention span of 24 minutes. Support your response with appropriate mathematical calculations.

solutions.latex:
The independent variable is the one that is chosen or explains the other.

Independent variable: average hours of sleep.

Dependent variable: average attention span.
Since $r = 0.8070$ is positive and close to $1$, the correlation is positive and strong.

criteria: Finds the gradient or the intercept correct to four decimal places, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Substitute $x = 12$ into the regression line.
$$\begin{aligned} y &= 1.2581\times 12 - 0.2527 \\ &= 14.84 \text{ minutes} \end{aligned}$$
This is extrapolation.
criteria: Finds the predicted value or states extrapolation, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Extrapolation as in source; the source does not state the data range, so not checked against the graph.

solutions.latex:
The gradient is $1.2581$.

For every extra 1 hour of average sleep per day, the average attention span increases by $1.2581$ minutes.

Substitute $y = 24$ into $y = 1.2581x - 0.2527$.
$$\begin{aligned} 24 &= 1.2581x - 0.2527 \\ 24.2527 &= 1.2581x \\ x &= 19.2772\ldots \end{aligned}$$
A student would not sleep approximately 19 hours per day, since they need to attend school for at least 6 to 7 hours. So the line is unreliable for this prediction.

parts.latex:
A set of bivariate data, was described to have a Pearson’s correlation coefficient of $r = -0.98$.

Which graph could best represent this set of bivariate data?

solutions.latex:
A correlation coefficient of $r=-0.98$ means a very strong negative linear relationship: the points trend downwards and lie almost exactly on a straight line.

Graphs A and C trend upwards (positive correlation), so they are rejected.

Graphs B and D both trend downwards. In graph D the points lie almost exactly on a straight line, so $r$ is very close to $-1$. In graph B the points are less linear (the last two have the same $x$ value), so $r$ is weaker.

Hence the correct option is D.

(The school accepted both B and D: $r$ is about $-0.92$ for B and about $-1.00$ for D, so D is the closer match.)

parts.latex:
Suppose a sixth data point was collected on a day which had 10 hours of sunshine. On that day 45 bottles of lemonade were sold.

What would happen to the gradient found in part (a)?

solutions.latex:
Using two points on the line, $(0,2)$ and $(5,18)$, the gradient is
$$\begin{aligned} m &= \dfrac{18-2}{5-0} \\ &= 3.2 \end{aligned}$$
The intercept is $2$.
$$\therefore\ y = 2 + 3.2x$$
criteria: Finds the intercept, finds the gradient, or writes down a linear equation

solutions.latex:
The point $(10, 45)$ lies above the line (the line gives $y = 2+3.2\times 10 = 34$ there), so the line is pulled upwards on the right.

Therefore the gradient would increase.

4470.stem:
For a sample of 17 inland towns in Australia, the height above sea level, $x$ (metres), and the average maximum daily temperature, $y$ ($^\circ$C), were recorded.

The graph shows the data as well as a regression line.

\exfigure{38_q33_1}

The equation of the regression line is $y = 29.2 - 0.011x$.

The correlation coefficient is $r = -0.494$.

figures.cap: scatterplot of temperature against height above sea level
scatterplot of temperature against latitude

parts.latex: By using the equation of the regression line, predict the average maximum daily temperature, in degrees Celsius, for a town that is 540 m above sea level. Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
The gradient of the regression line is $-0.011$. Interpret the value of this gradient in the given context.

The graph below shows the relationship between the latitude, $x$ (degrees south), and the average maximum daily temperature, $y$ ($^\circ$C), for the same 17 towns, as well as a regression line.

\exfigure{38_q33_2}

The equation of the regression line is $y = 45.6 - 0.683x$.

The correlation coefficient is $r = -0.897$.

Another inland town in Australia is 540 m above sea level. Its latitude is 28 degrees south.

Which measurement, height above sea level or latitude, would be better to use to predict this town’s average maximum daily temperature? Give a reason for your answer.

solutions.latex:
Substitute $x=540$ into the regression equation.
$$\begin{aligned} y &= 29.2 - 0.011\times 540 \\ &= 23.3^\circ\text{C} \end{aligned}$$
For a one metre increase in the height above sea level, we expect a $0.011^\circ\text{C}$ drop in average maximum daily temperature.
criteria: Provides a correct relevant statement relating temperature to height above sea level, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
It would be better to use the latitude.

From the information given, the average maximum daily temperature has a stronger correlation with latitude ($r=-0.897$) than with height above sea level ($r=-0.494$).

parts.latex: What is the equation of the least-squares regression line for this dataset?

Another student, whose marks are not on the graph, scored 5 for the assignment and 12 on the test.

Did this student do better or worse on the test than the regression line predicts? Provide a reason for your answer.

solutions.latex:
The gradient is
$$m=\dfrac{14}{10}=1.4$$
Hence the equation is
$$y=1.4x+6$$
criteria: Finds the $y$-intercept or gradient, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex: Worse, as the predicted test mark was $13$ instead of $12$.

parts.latex:
A researcher is studying anacondas (a type of snake).

A dataset recording the age (in years) and length (in cm) of female and male anacondas is displayed on the graph.

Anacondas reach maturity at about 4 years of age.

\exfigure{40_q30_1}

Write THREE observations about anacondas that may be made from the scatterplot. (Note: No calculations are required.)

solutions.latex:
Observations (any three):

Female anacondas grow at a faster rate than males.

Both females and males continue to grow after 4 years.

Females are longer than males.
criteria: Provides two correct observations, or equivalent merit
Provides one correct observation, or equivalent merit
